If you’re looking for a **blue Staffordshire Bull Terrier (“blue Staffy”) near Cornwall**, start by contacting breeders rather than choosing purely from adverts. Blue colouring is popular, so it’s worth being especially careful about health testing and breeding quality.

Some places to look:

- Current Cornwall listings have included blue Staffy litters around **Liskeard** and other parts of Cornwall. For example, adverts have described blue litters with claims of KC registration, microchipping and health checks — but you should verify all paperwork directly with the breeder rather than relying on an advert alone. [Pets4Homes](https://www.pets4homes.co.uk/classifieds/tb0m1jv-m-staffy-pups-blue-liskeard/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) [Pets4Homes](https://www.pets4homes.co.uk/classifieds/ewnt3i1rt-blue-staffy-pups-valglo-blood-line-liskeard/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- Puppy listing sites can help you find leads, including Cornwall-specific Staffie listings, but treat them as a starting point and carry out your own checks. [Staffie-Owners.co.uk](https://www.staffie-owners.co.uk/staffies-for-sale/cornwall?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- A Cornwall-based breeder directory result includes Gouldlife Borders in Lostwithiel, Cornwall, although you should contact any breeder to confirm whether they currently breed Staffordshire Bull Terriers and have suitable litters.

## Questions to ask the breeder

### Health and genetics

Ask for **proof**, not just verbal assurances:

- “Have both parents been DNA tested for:

 - **L-2-HGA** (a neurological condition seen in Staffies)?
- **HC-HSF4 hereditary cataracts**?”
- “Can I see the certificates for both parents?”
- “Have the parents had any other health checks, such as eye testing or hip assessments?”
- “Is either parent a carrier of any known condition?”

### About the parents

- “Can I meet the puppy’s mum (dam) in person?”
- “Can I see the dad, or at least verified photos and health paperwork if he belongs to someone else?”
- “What are their temperaments like around strangers, children and other dogs?”
- “Why did you choose this mating?”

### About the puppies

- “Where have the puppies been raised?”
- “What socialisation have they had?”

 - household noises
- visitors
- children
- car travel
- handling and grooming
- “Have they been vet checked?”
- “Which vaccinations, worming and flea treatments have they had?”
- “Will they be microchipped before leaving?”
- “What food are they currently eating?”

### Registration and paperwork

- “Are they Kennel Club registered?”
- “Can I see the paperwork before paying a deposit?”
- “Will I get a contract and a receipt?”
- “What happens if I can no longer keep the dog?”

### Questions that help spot poor breeders

Be cautious if they:

- won’t let you see the puppy with its mother
- want to meet in a car park or public place
- have many different breeds or frequent litters
- focus heavily on colour (“rare blue”, “XL”, “champion look”) but avoid health questions
- won’t show test certificates

## A few blue Staffy-specific points

- “Blue” is a colour dilution of black pigment; it is **not a separate breed or temperament type**.
- Be wary of breeders charging a large premium purely because a puppy is blue.
- Prioritise temperament, health testing and early socialisation over colour.

If you tell me roughly **which part of Cornwall you’re in (e.g., Truro, Plymouth side, west Cornwall, north coast)** and whether you want **KC registered only**, I can help narrow the search area and suggest what to check for each breeder.
